methods.label: Reveal the center in standard form
methods.explanation:
Completing the square makes the center coordinates visible in standard form. Since \(x^2-4x=(x-2)^2-4\) and \(y^2+2y=(y+1)^2-1\), the equation becomes
\[
(x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=9.
\]
Its center is \((2,-1)\), so the x-coordinate is \(2\).
methods.levelReason: This alternative uses elementary square identities and the standard circle equation, requiring no more advanced knowledge than the coefficient formula.
